Should you worry that choline, a nutrient found in eggs, is bad for your heart?

In 2013, a Cleveland Clinic study of about 4,000 heart patients linked TMAO (trimethylamine N-oxide), a compound gut bacteria make from choline, to heart attacks. Patients with the highest TMAO levels were much more likely to have a heart attack, a stroke or die over the next three years.

Later studies put that link to the test. In 2019, researchers used genetics: if TMAO causes heart disease, people born with genes that raise it should have more heart disease. They didn't. Diabetes and kidney disease push TMAO up, so it may simply mark people who are already unwell. In 2021, mice prone to clogged arteries were fed extra phosphatidylcholine. Their TMAO doubled, but they had less plaque in their arteries, not more. And as far as I can find, nobody has yet run a trial that lowers TMAO in people and then counts heart attacks.

Choline also comes in several forms. Phosphatidylcholine is the main form in food, a fat with choline attached. Supplements often use choline salts such as choline bitartrate. In a 2021 Cleveland Clinic trial lasting about four weeks, choline bitartrate pushed TMAO up, but phosphatidylcholine supplements didn't, and neither did four eggs a day.

TMAO hasn't been shown to cause heart attacks, and in that trial, eggs and phosphatidylcholine supplements didn't even raise it.

Consuming fructose can put a lot of stress on your liver.

outliers.descripcion:
Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology.

Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits.

Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time.

Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times.

To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment.

And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are.
